## Two functions, one model

`nowcaster` has two workhorse functions that fit the same model: a negative
binomial model for the delay triangle, with a smooth effect for the week of onset
and another for the reporting delay.

* `nowcasting_inla()` fits it in a fully Bayesian way with
  [`INLA`](https://www.r-inla.org/download-install), with random walk priors for
  the time and delay effects.
* `nowcasting_mgcv()` fits it as a generalised additive model with
  [`mgcv`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mgcv), with penalised splines for the
  time and delay effects.

Both take the same main arguments and return the same output, so switching from
one to the other is a matter of changing the function name. In this article each
example is shown for both functions: **use the tabs above each code block to
switch between them**. Choosing a tab switches all the examples on the page.

| | `nowcasting_inla()` | `nowcasting_mgcv()` |
|---|---|---|
| Fitting engine | `INLA` (not on CRAN) | `mgcv` (on CRAN, installed with `nowcaster`) |
| Time and delay effects | random walks (`rw2`, `rw1`) | penalised thin plate splines |
| Uncertainty | posterior samples of the latent field and hyperparameters | samples of the coefficients, dispersion fixed at its estimate |
| Extra options | `zero_inflated`, `timeREmodel`, `INLAoutput`, `WAIC`, `DIC` | `method.group.gam` |

## Data

```{r data}
library(nowcaster)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

data(sragBH)

# A helper to plot an estimate together with the curve observed at the time
plot_nowcast <- function(estimate, observed) {
  ggplot(estimate, aes(x = dt_event)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_line(aes(y = Median, colour = "Nowcasting")) +
    geom_line(data = observed, aes(y = observed, colour = "Observed")) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Nowcasting = "black", Observed = "grey50"),
                        name = "") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%V/%y") +
    labs(x = "Week of onset of symptoms", y = "Number of cases") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
}
```

## Nowcasting

### Fit {.tabset}

#### INLA

```{r no-age-inla}
now_inla <- nowcasting_inla(dataset = sragBH,
                            date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                            date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                            data.by.week = TRUE)
head(now_inla$total)
```

#### mgcv

```{r no-age-mgcv}
now_mgcv <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = sragBH,
                            date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                            date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                            data.by.week = TRUE)
head(now_mgcv$total)
```

### Plot {.tabset}

The delay triangle in the element `data` is the same for both functions; summing
over the delays gives the curve observed at the time of the last record.

#### INLA

```{r no-age-plot-inla}
observed <- now_inla$data |>
  group_by(dt_event) |>
  summarise(observed = sum(Y, na.rm = TRUE))

plot_nowcast(now_inla$total, observed)
```

#### mgcv

```{r no-age-plot-mgcv}
observed <- now_mgcv$data |>
  group_by(dt_event) |>
  summarise(observed = sum(Y, na.rm = TRUE))

plot_nowcast(now_mgcv$total, observed)
```

## Nowcasting by age

With `age_col` both functions fit the structured model, with time and delay
effects for each age class. `nowcasting_inla()` uses an independent effect per age
class for the random walks; `nowcasting_mgcv()` uses a factor smooth
(`method.group.gam = "fs"`, the default) or one smooth per age class
(`method.group.gam = "by"`).

### Fit {.tabset}

#### INLA

```{r age-inla}
now_age_inla <- nowcasting_inla(dataset = sragBH,
                                date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                                date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                                age_col = Idade,
                                bins_age = "10 years")
head(now_age_inla$age)
```

#### mgcv

```{r age-mgcv}
now_age_mgcv <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = sragBH,
                                date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                                date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                                age_col = Idade,
                                bins_age = "10 years")
head(now_age_mgcv$age)
```

## Forecasting

With `K > 0` both functions also forecast the weeks after the last onset week.
Here we cut the data on 4 July 2020 and forecast one week ahead.

```{r cut}
srag_2020 <- sragBH |>
  filter(DT_DIGITA <= as.Date("2020-07-04"))
```

### Fit {.tabset}

#### INLA

```{r forecast-inla}
fc_inla <- nowcasting_inla(dataset = srag_2020,
                           date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                           date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                           K = 1)
tail(fc_inla$total, 3)
```

#### mgcv

```{r forecast-mgcv}
fc_mgcv <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = srag_2020,
                           date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                           date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                           K = 1)
tail(fc_mgcv$total, 3)
```

## Comparing the estimates

Putting both estimates on the same plot, together with the curve that was
eventually observed, shows how close they are.

```{r compare}
eventually_observed <- sragBH |>
  mutate(dt_event = DT_SIN_PRI - as.numeric(format(DT_SIN_PRI, "%w"))) |>
  count(dt_event, name = "observed")

both <- bind_rows(
  fc_inla$total |> mutate(model = "nowcasting_inla()"),
  fc_mgcv$total |> mutate(model = "nowcasting_mgcv()")
)

ggplot(both, aes(x = dt_event)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS, fill = model), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Median, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(data = eventually_observed |>
              filter(dt_event >= min(both$dt_event),
                     dt_event <= max(both$dt_event)),
            aes(y = observed), colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("steelblue4", "darkorange3"), name = "") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("steelblue2", "darkorange1"), name = "") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%V/%y") +
  labs(x = "Week of onset of symptoms", y = "Number of cases",
       caption = "Dashed red line: cases eventually observed") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

The width of the 95% intervals in the most recent weeks:

```{r widths}
both |>
  group_by(model) |>
  slice_tail(n = 4) |>
  mutate(width_95 = LS - LI) |>
  select(model, dt_event, Median, LI, LS, width_95)
```

## Which one to use

* `nowcasting_mgcv()` needs only CRAN packages. It is a good
  default when `INLA` is not available or for routine use.
* `nowcasting_inla()` is the fully Bayesian version of the model. It propagates the
  uncertainty of all parameters, including the dispersion, and offers the options
  of the original model (zero-inflation, other latent models for time, model
  comparison with WAIC and DIC).

The two functions share the data preparation and the summary of the trajectories,
so differences between their estimates come from the model fit only.
